newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sets up body to upgrade private firms.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sets up body to upgrade private firms.

text.p: Morocco has set up a special team to supervise and help upgrade around 4,000 private firms to face increasing competition from Europe.

The official MAP news agency on Wednesday quoting Trade Minister Driss Jettou said: "The CMN (Comite de Mise a Niveau), which was set up by the trade ministry, has drawn up an urgent plan to upgrade Morocco's private firms."

Morocco last year signed an agreement with the European Union to establish a free trade zone by the year 2010. Officials said they expected the CMN to take urgent measures to modernise and strengthen up to 4,000 private firms in a 12-year plan.
"Construction of industrial areas and development of technology infrastructures are among the plan's priorities," MAP quoted Jettou as saying.
Investments in Morocco's electronic technology sector jumped to more than 700 million dirhams ($75.3 million) in 1996 from 15 million dirhams in 1992, Jettou said.
"It is expected that South Korean Daewoo firm will invest $200 million over a three-year period to build television sets near Casablanca airport," the minister said.
The Daewoo conglomerate, which is expanding its business activity in North Africa, last year bought Morocco's five-star Hyatt Regency hotel for $28.7 million.
According to the minister, French SGS Thomson group, which owns a plant producing electronic components in Casablanca, plans to invest $300 million in a five-year plan.

"These investments allow a transfer of technology and will have a positive impact on human resources...With the future free-trade zone with the EU, Morocco will have other opportunities with positive repercussions on exports," the minister added.
He did not say when the French and Korean investments would be effective.
